response:
Losing a friendship after 20 years is a real loss, and it makes sense that you're feeling depressed and anxious. That history matters, and the mixed signals—sometimes open, sometimes distant and angry—can leave you feeling confused and stuck, unsure whether to hold on or let go.

The hard truth is that friendship takes two people who both want it, and you can't force someone to stay. But you don't have to give up without trying to understand what's happening. If you haven't already, it may help to gently and directly ask her what she needs, and whether she genuinely wants to work things out. That gives you clarity, even if the answer hurts.

Whatever she decides, please take care of your own wellbeing too. Lean on other people who care about you, and if the depression or anxiety feels heavy or hard to manage, talking with a counselor could really help. You deserve support through this.
